title: Fabrication of Zero Mode Waveguides for High Concentration Single Molecule Microscopy
protocol: Place 24 x 30 mm optical borosilicate glass coverslips within the grooved inserts of a coplin glass staining jar for cleaning.
Pour acetone into the staining jar to cover the coverslips, place the cover on, and sonicate for 10 min at 40 °C.
Pour out the acetone and rinse the coverslips by filling the staining jar with distilled H2O and pouring out the water. Repeat twice more.
Repeat the acetone sonication once more.
Pour 200 mM KOH into the jar to cover the coverslips, sonicate covered for 20 min at 40 °C.
Rinse the coverslips with distilled H2O six times.
Add ethanol to cover the coverslips, add the lid, and sonicate for 10 min at 40 °C.
Rinse the coverslips with distilled H2O three times.
Dry the coverslips with N2 gas by picking up each coverslip at the edge using gentle forceps.
Place each of the dried, cleaned coverslips in an individual clean Petri dish.
Centrifuge 50 μl of 1 µm diameter, non-functionalized polystyrene beads (2.5% w/v in water) at 15,000 x g, 25 °C for 5 min.
Vortex the stock solution briefly before pipetting to resuspend the beads.
Discard the supernatant, leaving as little water remaining as possible.
Resuspend the beads in 50 μl of 1:400 TritonX-100:ethanol solvent.
Pipette up and down several times to thoroughly mix the beads with the solvent.
Place 6 Petri dishes on a bench in a line with lids left slightly ajar.
Move the coverslip to the open region in each dish so that they are exposed to the environment.
Place a hygrometer and a small electric fan centered behind the Petri dishes.
Record the starting relative humidity (RH) in the lab.
Fill a 200 mL beaker with 150−200 mL of ~75 °C water and place it behind the fan.
Turn on the fan.
Cover the Petri dishes, fan, beaker, and hygrometer with an overturned, transparent plastic storage container (66 cm x 46 cm x 38 cm).
Let the RH in the chamber rise to 70−75%, which typically takes 5−10 min.
Record the RH when it reaches 70−75%.
Lift up the plastic storage container slightly to quickly place covers on the Petri dishes, preventing over-wetting of the coverslips.
Let the RH in the chamber continue to rise to 85%.
Record the RH in the humidity chamber after reaching 85%.
Pipette 5 µL of the bead suspension onto the center of each coverslip.
Close the chamber and Petri dishes after each deposition to minimize loss of humidity.
Aim to finish all 6 depositions within 2 min.
Record the RH in the chamber after the deposition.
Place a flat, milled aluminum plate on top of a standard ceramic hot plate.
Set the temperature of the hot plate to 107 °C.
Place a coverslip containing the bead template on the hot aluminum plate and anneal for 20 s.
Remove the coverslip from the aluminum plate after heating.
Promptly place the heated coverslip on another room temperature aluminum surface to cool it.
Deposit 300 nm of copper at 2 Å/s over the colloidal crystal template using thermal or electron-beam evaporative deposition.
Remove excess metal on top of the beads by gently pressing the surface with tape.
Slowly peel the tape to pull off the metal.
Wash the coverslips with distilled water, dry with N2, and repeat the tape pull if necessary.
Soak the templates in toluene overnight for 2 hours to partially dissolve polystyrene beads if substantial patches of reflective excess metal remain after the tape pull.
Work with toluene under a well-ventilated hood and wear personal protective equipment including gloves, safety glasses, and a lab coat.
Rinse templates once with chloroform.
Rinse templates twice with ethanol.
Dry templates with N₂.
Remove residual polymer and contaminants using an oxygen plasma cleaner for 30 min.
Deposit 3 nm of titanium adhesion layer at 1 Å/s.
Deposit 100−150 nm of aluminum at 4 Å/s around and on top of the copper posts.
Soak coverslips in copper etchant for 2 h to dissolve metal posts.
Rinse the coverslips with distilled water.
Dry the coverslips with N2.
Gently buff the surface of the metal cladding with lens paper to expose any posts that are still covered in cladding.
Place the coverslips back in copper etchant for another 2 h.
Rinse the coverslips again with distilled water.
Dry the coverslips with N2.
Store ZMW slides in covered, clean Petri dishes to keep them free of contaminants.
Deposit 3 nm of titanium adhesion layer at 1 Å/s using thermal or electron beam evaporative deposition.
Deposit 300 nm of aluminum at 4 Å/s using thermal or electron beam evaporative deposition.
Remove excess metal on top of the beads by gently pressing the surface with tape.
Slowly peel the tape to pull off the metal.
Place the bead templates in toluene and soak overnight to dissolve polystyrene beads.
Rinse the templates once with chloroform after the toluene incubation.
Rinse the templates twice with ethanol.
Dry the templates with N2.
Remove residual polymer contaminants in an oxygen plasma cleaner for 30 min.
Deposit 100−150 nm of gold at 5 Å/s around and on top of the aluminum posts using thermal or electron beam evaporative deposition.
Soak the coverslips in aluminum etchant for 1 hour.
Rinse the coverslips with distilled water.
Dry the coverslips with N2.
Gently buff the surface of the metal cladding with lens paper to expose any posts that are still covered in cladding.
Place the coverslips back in aluminum etchant for 1 hour.
Rinse the coverslips again with distilled water.
Dry the coverslips with N2.
